# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 40 (Bu-Vb Sk40)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 40, titled *Parimaṇḍala* ("Not making rounded mouthfuls" in Bhikkhu Sujato's rendering), is a training rule from the Sekhiya section of the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic etiquette while taking food [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Full parallels to this rule are preserved widely across early Buddhist Vinaya traditions, occurring in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Sekhiya 40), both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas, and the Parivāra, as well as in the monastic codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, and Upāliparipṛcchā lineages preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. Resembling parallels are also recognized by SuttaCentral in Sekhiya 39 (*Nātimahanta*) across multiple Vinayas [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus records 131 instances of Pali-internal text reuse across 49 texts, sharing the highest textual overlap and stock formulaic phrasing with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 39 (§0.1–1.17, similarity 0.89) alongside other Sekhiya rules including Sekhiya 18, 31, and 20 [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
